CASSCF reproduces the 1 pi-pi* vertical excitation reasonably but overestimates the 2 pi-pi* vertical excitation by 1.96 eV because of its charge-transfer character, which wrongly places the 2 pi-sigma* state below 2 pi-pi*; XMCQDPT2 restores the correct ordering. XMCQDPT2 with CAS2 plus the two 3p Rydberg orbitals puts the 3pz and 3py states at 5.58 and 5.62 eV, slightly above the 2 pi-pi* state, contradicting CR-EOM-CCSD(T) values of 5.31 and 5.42 eV that had placed them between 1 pi-sigma* and 2 pi-pi*. Adding the ligand HOMO and LUMO to the active space barely changes the relative state energies (columns marked with a dagger), showing the ligand HOMO stays doubly occupied and the LUMO empty even though the metal-centred orbitals lie well below the ligand HOMO; this can only happen if the cost of pairing electrons in the compact metal d orbitals exceeds the cost of placing and pairing them in the ligand HOMO.

basis_set: 6-31G(d) for geometry optimization, 6-31+G(d) for excited-state calculations
active_space_orbital_description: all orbitals selected by the unrestricted natural orbital occupation criterion plus additional pi orbitals of the conjugated chromophore
active_space_protocol: unrestricted natural orbitals (UNOs) used as the initial guess and as the automatic active-space selector: include all orbitals with natural occupation numbers between 0.01 and 1.99, reducing the set if the resulting space is too large. compound_name: Free d- and f-block metal ions (3d, 4d and 5d transition metal ions in various oxidation states, and trivalent lanthanide ions), assessed as a minimal-active-space reference set
metal_center: 3d, 4d and 5d transition metals and trivalent f-block ions (Eu(III), Gd(III) and Tb(III) excluded for cost)
metal_ox_state: various, spanning the common oxidation states of each block; trivalent for the f-block ions
d_electron_count: all dn configurations for the transition metal ions and all fn configurations for the trivalent lanthanides
point_group: spherical symmetry enforced with the ATOM supersymmetry keyword for the optimized atomic orbitals
geometry_source: free ions, no geometry
method: minimal active space CASSCF-SO: state-averaged CASSCF followed by state interaction with spin-orbit coupling; MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2 additionally performed for Co(II) and Pr(III) to show the effect of dynamic correlation; results recast into Slater-Condon and spin-orbit coupling parameters in the Russell-Saunders basis and compared with experiment, AILFT and ligand-field DFT
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic Hamiltonian (two-component decoupling of the four-component Dirac Hamiltonian) with atomic mean-field integrals (AMFI) for the spin-orbit Hamiltonian
soc_included: yes, spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction after variational spin-free orbital optimization
active_space_orbital_description: the minimal active space: n electrons in the five d orbitals for the d-block, or n electrons in the seven f orbitals for the f-block, where n is the dn or fn configuration of the ion
active_space_protocol: minimal active space, (n,5) for d-block ions and (n,7) for f-block ions, state-averaged over all possible roots for every spin multiplicity of the given configuration; (X)MS-CASPT2 on all SA-CASSCF roots with an imaginary shift of 0.1 for the Co(II) and Pr(III) comparisons
multiplicities_studied: all possible spin multiplicities of each dn or fn configuration
nroots_per_mult: all roots of each configuration and multiplicity
Other: This is the reference assessment of when the ubiquitous minimal active space is good enough. Spin-orbit coupling constants: reproduced to within about 200 cm-1 of experimentally derived values, which is usually under 10 percent error for 4dn, 5dn and 4fn configurations but up to 30 percent for 3dn; the abstract-level summary is overestimation by 5-30 percent for 3d ions, within plus or minus 10 percent for 4d and 5d ions, and overestimation by 2-10 percent for trivalent 4f ions. Slater-Condon parameters are typically overestimated by 20-50 percent (with some 3d outliers underestimated by 1-20 percent) because of the missing dynamic correlation, so the authors explicitly do not recommend minimal active space CASSCF-SO where accurate term excitation energies are needed, and recommend CASPT2 or NEVPT2 instead for quantitative work. The Slater-Condon error is systematic for divalent 4d and trivalent 4f ions, so simple scaling may be viable there when resources are limited, but this does not hold for 3d ions. The spin-orbit coupling constant varies quadratically with atomic number Z at fixed dn configuration, and also for the trivalent lanthanides even though the configuration changes with Z
reference_short: Walisinghe and Chilton, Assessment of minimal active space CASSCF-SO methods for calculation of atomic Slater-Condon and spin-orbit coupling parameters in d- and f-block ions, Dalton Trans. 50, 14130 (2021)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Free ions rather than coordination compounds, and covering many ions at once, so this is entered as a single reference row rather than one row per ion; active_space_nel is left empty because it varies with the ion. Directly relevant to active-space selection: it quantifies the accuracy ceiling of the (n,5)/(n,7) minimal space that underpins most single_aniso and AILFT work on real complexes.

ligand_set: three bidentate acetylacetonate (acac) chelates, pseudo-octahedral O6
geometry_source: optimized with Kohn-Sham DFT using the revM06-L functional and def2-TZVP basis, with frequency analysis confirming a local minimum; gas phase
method: two-stage spin-orbit-inclusive multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory: stage one is spin-orbit-free CASCI or CMS-PDFT on two spin manifolds using orbitals from CASSCF, SA-CASSCF or WSA-CASSCF; stage two adds spin-orbit coupling by state interaction (RASSI) over all degenerate components of the retained roots
software: OpenMolcas 21.02 for the multiconfigurational calculations; locally modified Gaussian 16 Revision C.01 for the DFT geometries
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VTZP for the transition metal, oxygen and nitrogen; ANO-RCC-VDZP for carbon; ANO-RCC-MB for hydrogen and fluorine; auxiliary basis sets for the two-electron integrals; def2-TZVP for the DFT geometries
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH2) for the scalar relativistic terms
soc_included: yes, added by state interaction over the two spin manifolds after spin-orbit-free orbital optimization
active_space_orbital_description: the valence d electrons in the five metal d orbitals
active_space_protocol: (2,5) valence-d minimal space used identically for CASSCF, SA-CASSCF and WSA-CASSCF; the three orbital-optimization schemes differ only in the state weighting, with WSA-CASSCF putting 90 percent weight on the lowest state of each spin manifold and spreading 10 percent over the rest. For V(acac)3 all five d orbitals are retained even by state-specific CASSCF.
nroots_per_mult: 15 singlet and 10 triplet roots carried into the spin-orbit state interaction
low_lying_states_eV: Zero-field splitting D (cm-1), SA-CASSCF/CASCI -13.64, SA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 13.85, CASSCF/CASCI 4.90, CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 4.96, WSA-CASSCF/CASCI 6.82, WSA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 7.75, experiment 7.47
Other: Spin-orbit lowering of the ground state: -35 cm-1 with SA-CASSCF orbitals, -15 with CASSCF, -19 with WSA-CASSCF; SA-CASSCF badly overestimates the SOC contribution here and even gets the sign of D wrong. One of the three molecules used for the ground-state-weight sensitivity scan, which shows a discontinuous jump in D near 25 percent weight. Core finding of the study, which is about how the orbitals are optimized rather than about the active space size: state-specific CASSCF orbitals beat conventional equal-weight SA-CASSCF orbitals, but state-specific optimization can rotate d orbitals that are empty in the ground state out of the active space entirely (this happens for Cr(acac)3 and Mo(acac)3, where two unoccupied d orbitals are lost even from a good initial guess, although the SCF itself converges). The proposed weighted-state-averaged CASSCF fixes this by putting 90 percent of the weight on the lowest state of each spin manifold and spreading the remaining 10 percent evenly over the others; all five d orbitals are then retained. Mean percentage absolute deviation in D across the set: SA-CASSCF/CASCI 102 percent, SA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 138, CASSCF/CASCI 39, CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 90, WSA-CASSCF/CASCI 27, and WSA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 14 percent (mean percentage deviation 3 percent), making WSA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT the recommended combination. The ground-state weight can be anywhere from 50 to 95 percent without significantly changing D. Fe(acac)3 is excluded from the mean errors because its experimental D is near zero. Geometry and solvation tests on Mn(acac)3 show that DFT-optimized gas-phase structures give essentially the same D as experimental structures.
reference_short: Wu, Zhou, Bao, Gagliardi and Truhlar, Zero-Field Splitting Calculations by Multiconfiguration Pair-Density Functional Theory, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2022)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Oxidation state and d-electron count follow arithmetically from the ligand charges and the stated active-space electron count. One of the two cases where conventional SA-CASSCF gives qualitatively wrong D. Note the paper writes the ligand as hfa (1,1,1,5,5,5-hexafluoro-2,4-pentanedione) in the abstract but hfc in the tables; the table spelling is kept here for traceability.

compound_name: Coelenterazine (CTZ) dioxetanone, the reactive bioluminescent intermediate, in the NanoLuc luciferase protein (also computed in the gas phase and in PCM for comparison)
geometry_source: QM/MM optimized in this work. The protein-solvent system was equilibrated for 10 ns of classical AMOEBA MD, the CTZ+O2 coordinates were then manually replaced by the dioxetanone, and only a 932-atom relaxed region around the chromophore was optimized (rest frozen at the snapshot); QM region 177 atoms, comprising the chromophore plus hydrogen-bonding side chains. Reactant and product were also optimized separately in the gas phase and in PCM (eps = 78.4). Reaction path by interpolation between the optimized reactant and product for each environment
method: SA-CASSCF with polarizable QM/MM embedding in the AMOEBA force field (SA-CASSCF/AMOEBA), dynamically weighted with S0 as reference state and a 3 eV bandwidth in the PCM and QM/MM calculations; minimum-energy conical intersection searches on top
software: TeraChem for the QM part coupled to OpenMM for the MM part
active_space_orbital_description: chosen to contain enough active orbitals to describe the O-O bond dissociation of the dioxetanone ring; the low-lying states it produces are n->sigma* and sigma->sigma* local excitations in the O-O bond region
active_space_protocol: (8,9) sized around the breaking O-O bond; state-averaging over four singlets and two triplets, with dynamic weights referenced to S0 using a 3 eV bandwidth. A separate, much smaller SA(2)-CASSCF(4,3)/3-21G space was used only on an HBDI-valine model to parametrize the force field and to compare link-atom schemes
nroots_per_mult: 4 singlets and 2 triplets in the state-average
Other: State characters from attach-detach density analysis at image 20 of the gas-phase path: S1, S2 and S3 are all local 1(n,sigma*) excitations in the O-O region; T1 is 3(n,sigma*) and T2 is 3(sigma,sigma*). Environment changes the picture qualitatively. In the gas phase and in PCM the S1-S0 gap closes as the O-O bond dissociates and the MECI geometry closely resembles the product; in QM/MM the S1-S0 gap no longer approaches zero along the path, S2 and S3 rise well above their gas-phase positions (they acquire core-region excitation character), and reaching the MECI requires rotating the O-C-O group by almost 90 degrees out of the dioxetanone ring plane. The MECI topology also differs: peaked in PCM, sloped in QM/MM. Protonation: unconstrained QM/MM optimization always ends with HPh protonated and D139 deprotonated; forcing the deprotonated state requires O-H distance constraints and costs 15.6 kcal/mol. The proton-transfer energy computed with AMOEBA embedding is less sensitive to QM-region size than with a fixed-charge (AMBER-FB15 / SPC-Fw / GAFF) model.
reference_short: A Polarizable QM/MM Model That Combines the State-Averaged CASSCF and AMOEBA Force Field for Photoreactions in Proteins, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2024)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Metal-free organic (metal_center = none).
